name: Elijah
overview: Elijah was a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as the son of Harim who had married a foreign wife, as noted in Ezra 10:21. His background places him within the Levitical lineage, which carried significant religious responsibilities in Israel. Beyond this unique attribute, there are no additional personal notes recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Elijah means 'y-h-v-h is [my] G-d,' reflecting a declaration of faith in the LORD. This proper name highlights the centrality of God in his identity and mission, as documented in Ezra 10:21.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Elijah as a descendant of Harim, establishing a direct familial link within the tribe of Levi. No other family relationships are detailed beyond this connection and his identification as the son of Harim who had taken a foreign wife.
scriptureSignificance: Elijah is a pivotal prophetic figure who emerged during a period of apostasy in Israel, boldly confronting idolatry and leading the people back to the true God. His ministry included dramatic displays of God's power, such as calling down fire from heaven and initiating a drought, demonstrating divine authority. Elijah's life culminated in a unique departure from earth, being taken to heaven in a whirlwind, underscoring his exceptional role in God's redemptive plan. He also foreshadows Christ and the prophetic witness culminating in the New Testament, appearing with Moses at the transfiguration and being linked to the prophetic fulfillment in John the Baptist.
